items.description:
Payment Subscriptions allow you to charge customers recurringly for access to a product or service. Edge supports subscriptions with billing cycles `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `bimonthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual`, and `yearly`. Edge will create a new charge against the associated payment method when a new cycle begins.

For subscriptions configured with `proration_behavior: create_prorations` and a future `billing_cycle_anchor_at`, Edge creates an immediate first-cycle prorated charge and keeps the anchor date for the first full recurring cycle.

### Events

You can listen to `payment_subscriptions.created`, `payment_subscriptions.updated` and `payment_subscriptions.deleted` events on the resource. In addition, charges would trigger their respective events as they advance through their lifecycle.

### Detecting Failures

A subscription will be in an `active` status unless specified otherwise. However, the customer may have entered the card details incorrectly. In this case, the subscription `status` will transit from `active` to `past_due`. Track this transition using `WebhookSubscription` by listening to the `subscription.updated` event.

items.description:
A `RefundDemand` instance signifies an attempt to refund a `PaymentDemand`.

  ### Partial refunds

  A payment demand may be refunded more than once, so long as the refunds
  together do not exceed its total. Omit `amount_cents` to refund the whole
  remaining balance; supply it to refund part of it.

  Refunds still in flight are counted against the remaining balance, so a
  refund that is pending or processing reserves its amount until it succeeds
  or fails.

  `amount_currency` is inherited from the payment demand and cannot be chosen.

  ### Idempotency

  Send an `idempotency_key` to make a refund request safe to retry. Repeating a
  request with the same key returns the refund the first one created rather
  than refunding again - including when the original consumed the whole
  balance. Reusing a key with different attributes is rejected. Keys are scoped
  to your merchant, and a request sent without one cannot be replayed.

attributes.description: Members of the attributes object (`attributes`) represent information about the resource object in which it's defined.

amount_cents.description: How much to refund, in cents. Omit to refund the full remaining balance. Must be greater than zero and no more than the payment's unrefunded amount.

amount_currency.description: The currency of the refund demand (ISO 4217). Inherited from the payment demand; read-only.

idempotency_key.description: A unique value that prevents the same request being processed twice. Scoped to your merchant; reusing a key replays the original operation.

data.description:
A `Payment Demand` instance signifies an attempt to transfer money from a customer's payment method to your Edge merchant account.

A payment demand optionally belongs to a `customer`, but it is recommended to associate a payment demand with the customer. Customer payment demand history can be used as evidence in case of a chargeback or dispute.

### Pre-authorization / Hold

Pre-authorization holds a certain amount from the customer's card. Such authorizations must be captured within 7 days time, or the hold will be removed.

You can opt into a pre-authorization by creating a payment demand with the `capture_method` attribute set to `manual`.

### Refund a payment demand

TODO: Fill this out

### Events

A payment demand through its lifecycle will emit events. You can listen to these events as webhooks through `WebhookSubscription`.

- `payment_demand.created`
- `payment_demand.updated`
- `payment_demand.refunded`
- `payment_demand.succeeded`
- `payment_demand.failed`
- `payment_demand.disputed`
- `payment_demand.deleted`

amount_refunded_cents.description: Total refunded so far, in cents. Server managed. Counts succeeded refunds only - refunds still in flight are not included, so this is not the refundable balance. A payment is fully refunded when `processor_state` is `refunded`.

data.description:
Payment Subscriptions allow you to charge customers recurringly for access to a product or service. Edge supports subscriptions with billing cycles `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `bimonthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual`, and `yearly`. Edge will create a new charge against the associated payment method when a new cycle begins.

For subscriptions configured with `proration_behavior: create_prorations` and a future `billing_cycle_anchor_at`, Edge creates an immediate first-cycle prorated charge and keeps the anchor date for the first full recurring cycle.

### Events

You can listen to `payment_subscriptions.created`, `payment_subscriptions.updated` and `payment_subscriptions.deleted` events on the resource. In addition, charges would trigger their respective events as they advance through their lifecycle.

### Detecting Failures

A subscription will be in an `active` status unless specified otherwise. However, the customer may have entered the card details incorrectly. In this case, the subscription `status` will transit from `active` to `past_due`. Track this transition using `WebhookSubscription` by listening to the `subscription.updated` event.

data.description:
A `RefundDemand` instance signifies an attempt to refund a `PaymentDemand`.

  ### Partial refunds

  A payment demand may be refunded more than once, so long as the refunds
  together do not exceed its total. Omit `amount_cents` to refund the whole
  remaining balance; supply it to refund part of it.

  Refunds still in flight are counted against the remaining balance, so a
  refund that is pending or processing reserves its amount until it succeeds
  or fails.

  `amount_currency` is inherited from the payment demand and cannot be chosen.

  ### Idempotency

  Send an `idempotency_key` to make a refund request safe to retry. Repeating a
  request with the same key returns the refund the first one created rather
  than refunding again - including when the original consumed the whole
  balance. Reusing a key with different attributes is rejected. Keys are scoped
  to your merchant, and a request sent without one cannot be replayed.

attributes.description: Members of the attributes object (`attributes`) represent information about the resource object in which it's defined.

amount_cents.description: How much to refund, in cents. Omit to refund the full remaining balance. Must be greater than zero and no more than the payment's unrefunded amount.

amount_currency.description: The currency of the refund demand (ISO 4217). Inherited from the payment demand; read-only.

idempotency_key.description: A unique value that prevents the same request being processed twice. Scoped to your merchant; reusing a key replays the original operation.
